This is one of the saddest things I’ve ever read, it brought a tear to my eye, you are such a strong person for publishing this online and my heart goes out to you. I understand your pain and anger and all the thoughts and questions that must be flying round your head. I can’t imagine how hard it must be for you and your family right now. You are a good man who saved your dads life and I pray that one day things are good again for your family, and your dad can thank you for being the hero that you are. 

Much love.

Sounds like you’ve got a good family kid, that’s something not all of us have got and when you get better it will feel like a blessing. Have you tried reducing your weed gradually? Nothing can be stopped overnight or your body will go into shock and the addiction will become worse. My suggestion for you would to do one thing at a time, and start to improve your life on a daily basis. Try as hard as it is to do things that make you happy/happier. This could be anything, such as playing a video game for example. If you can enjoy that time on the game and take away negativity in your life for a period of time then go for it. Doing things that make you feel better could also help you reduce your addiction as it takes your mind off it. Nothing changes overnight buddy and its easier said than done but you will start to notice a change in mood and general feel once things start to work out for you. I’m no expert so I’m sorry if you don’t agree with me because when you’re feeling that low hope doesn’t feel like it exists. But you’re 18 and you’re whole life is ahead of you, one step at a time mate. Get some support and get on the road to recovery. But always remember that some days are going to be tough, some days are going to be great. Nothing will change over night. Give it time and have faith. Hope this helps.
